slides.sub: For the first week or two

sections.heading: 1. Less bend, gradual return
lines: ① Wear shoes with a stiffer sole.
② If swollen: elevate and ice 10–15 min.
③ Tape to limit how far it bends.
④ Toe raises and hops only when comfy.

sections.heading: 2. Stop if…
lines: You can't put weight on it, it swells a lot,
or the toe looks odd — stop and get advice.

caption:
Lulu plays weekend footy on synthetic turf, and now the big toe twinges every time he pushes off.

When the big toe bends back hard, the joint can sprain. This is often called turf toe. Firm surfaces and soft, bendy shoes can make it more likely.

Hybi's plan for the first week or two: stiffer-soled shoes, elevate and ice for 10–15 minutes if it's swollen, tape to limit the bend, and bring back toe raises and hops only when they feel comfortable.

A pop at the time, lots of bruising or swelling, or no improvement after two weeks are worth an assessment. Our Chatswood and Sydney CBD physios can help. Book online via the link in bio ⚽
